why: Rule 1: both prongs rise away at a 38 deg V -- the 188 cm muon Braggs at 18000 (117k, p4 shows the template fall) and the 36 cm hadron chain Braggs at 18004 (158k), and 18001 is the cool minimum and lowest-z point of the chain.

Rule 1 plus rule 6: deg-3 junction at the dQ/dx minimum of the 290 cm track, with a short downward stub and a 55 cm low-dQ/dx shower starting a few cm above it; dropped a tier because the two track prongs leave at 178 deg (collinearity trap).

Rule 6/7: a knot of stopping protons (14.3 cm p Bragg 159k at 83066, 2.1 cm p at 233k) with the 49 cm all-electron cluster 6 opening as an ~11 deg cone whose axis extrapolates back through 83070 to under 1 deg, 30 cm upstream of the conversion.

Rule 1 with two Bragg ends: p4 shows the 67.7 cm muon rising to 400k at 11003 and the 5.1 cm proton rising to 210k at 11000, both cooling to MIP at 11002, and the prong pair is 138 deg so the single-scatter reading is excluded.
Rule 1 on a two-proton vertex: p4 shows both segments falling monotonically from their outer Bragg ends (220k at 23000, 198k near 23003) to ~125k at 23002, which they leave in a wide 61 deg V.

Rule 1: 2 of 3 prongs rise away from the dQ/dx minimum (33k) of the long track, and the 48 cm shower back-extrapolates to within 2 cm of 15004 across an 11.6 cm conversion gap; tier dropped because the two track prongs are 180 deg collinear.

Rule 8 territory: the whole event is two isolated sub-cm blobs 311 cm apart with no segments, no direction and no dQ/dx structure; 23000 is picked only because 24002 sits 3.6 cm from the downstream z face, so this is close to a guess.

Rule 1: both prongs rise away from 9000 (104k rising to 120k toward 9001, and to 220k in the 41-cluster stub), and the residual-range/dQ-dx match only works as two protons of ~16 cm and ~4 cm, not as one 20 cm track; tier dropped for the 178 deg prong pair.

Rule 1 on a single stopping heavy track: the chain 9001-9000-41016-41017 rises monotonically (100k, 107k, 367k) to the Bragg tip at 41017, the zoom shows the only blue/green points at the 9001 end, and no second prong leaves anywhere, so the track cools toward 9001.

Rule 1 with two Bragg ends, seen as a clean 90 deg V in X-Z: the 168 cm muon is flat MIP through the 11004 break and Braggs at 11000, while the 12.8 cm proton rises monotonically to 290k at 11001; the hot last bin at 11003 is vertex overlap, not a Bragg.

Rule 1 once vertex overlap is discounted: p4 shows the 12.9 cm proton falling monotonically from 295k at 9000 down to 135k at 9002, and the 72.6 cm muon flat at MIP with only a single hot point at arc 0, so the apparent rise toward 9002 is the proton's charge.

The only Bragg is at 7000, so the long track must start at its upstream low-z end, which frays into a 33 cm spray; 50048 is that fray's apex by the p5 cone (monotone 0.2 to 3.1 cm) -- but 7002's 2-of-2 rule-1 reading is a 180 deg collinear break and the track may simply run on to the anode, so this is weak.

Rule 1 plus shower pointing: two protons leave 83062 in a 98 deg V (15.4 cm to a 162k Bragg at 83061, 2.9 cm at 223k), and the 38 cm electron-segment shower axis passes 1.6 cm from 83062 versus 6.4 cm from the competing start at 84064.

52046 is the dQ/dx discontinuity (84k proton side versus 49k MIP side) where the 7.5 cm proton stopping at 52038 starts, and the 23 cm MIP track of cluster 4 back-extrapolates to it within 5 deg across a ~23 cm photon-conversion gap; 4000 is a phantom endpoint with no charge on it.
